messages:
claire: Storm took the neighborhood grid but my little off-grid plan worked. solar battery pack + old router in the shed = micro office. pics soon.
samir: Shed office?? this is legendary. pics pls :camera_with_flash: 
claire: uploaded: https://files.slack.com/files-pri/T12345-FABC01/shed-desk.jpg (yes the desk is a milk crate)
jun: how's latency on the solar-battery hotspot?
claire: about 150ms, 5 Mbps down / 1.8 Mbps up. fine for audio + terminal work. had to lower MTU to avoid fragmentation on the provider.
mika: pro tip: run `sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_forward=1`? kidding. but do monitor CPU on the router, mobile devices hate sustained NAT.
claire: ran `ip -s link` and the travel router's CPU spiked during file sync. paused Dropbox and things smoothed.
infra-bot: Reminder: please do not bridge personal APs to corporate networks. If you must do critical work, request an infra temporary VPN endpoint.
samir: we should make an "Emergency WFH kit" pinned doc: solar pack, ethernet, duct tape, milk crate desk, snacks. vote? :ballot_box_with_ballot:
jun: +1, add a section: "what not to do" (eg. don't leave the battery on the floor near puddles).
mika: also add a short checklist for router settings (MTU, disable IPv6 if flaky, keepalive tweaks).
claire: adding photos and a 2-line how-to later. TL;DR: you can work from a shed if you bring cable, patience, and snacks.
samir: post the pics to random gallery pls. this is peak content :laughing:
claire: one more pic from inside the shed trunk: https://files.slack.com/files-pri/T12345-FABC02/shed-router-closeup.jpg
